study_identification_part.si_4_title: Heterogeneity of morphometric similarity networks in health and schizophrenia

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Eleven datasets were combined: Amsterdam Open MRI Collection (aomic: id1000 N=927, piop1 N=209, piop2 N=224), Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (camcan N=645), Dallas Longitudinal Brain Study (dlbs N=309), Information eXtraction from Images (ixi N=456), Narratives (narratives N=336), Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (oasis3 N=615), NKI-Rockland (rockland N=495), Southwest University adult lifespan (sald N=494), and a longitudinal clinical dataset from Utrecht Schizophrenia project and GROUP consortium (N=459 at baseline: 292 HC + 167 SZ). Note: aomic, dlbs, narratives, and sald do not have standardized category names in the provided dataset list.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Eleven datasets were combined to create the full sample... We included healthy participants from ten publicly available datasets: the Amsterdam Open MRI Collection (aomic) (id1000, piop1 and piop2) datasets, the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (camcan) dataset, the Dallas Longitudinal Brain Study (dlbs) dataset, the Information eXtraction from Images (ixi) dataset, the Narratives (narratives) dataset, the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (oasis3) dataset, the NKI-Rockland (rockland) dataset and the Southwest University adult lifespan (sald) dataset. One dataset is not publicly available and consisted of a large longitudinal sample of individuals with schizophrenia and healthy participants aged 16-68 years (at baseline) from the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Janssen2024.pdf.md: MATERIALS AND METHODS / Sample, L52-54

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Ten publicly available datasets containing healthy controls were each split into training (~90%) and test (~10%) sets. The clinical dataset (Utrecht Schizophrenia project/GROUP) was split differently: all individuals with schizophrenia were included in the test set only for clinical application, while 20% of healthy controls went to training and 80% to test. The training set totaled 4310 participants and the test set 859 participants.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "For normative modeling, each of the ten datasets containing only healthy controls was split into a training set (≈90%) and a test set (≈10%). Following recommendations by ref. 7 and as for example in refs. 27,31,32, only healthy controls were included in the training set. For the clinical dataset, all individuals with schizophrenia, as well as 80% of the healthy controls, were included in the test set, while the remaining healthy controls (20%) were included in the training set... The training set included 4310 participants and the test set 859 participants."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Janssen2024.pdf.md: MATERIALS AND METHODS / Normative modeling of morphometric similarity, L117

model-1.model-name: morphometric similarity normative model (Bayesian linear regression with likelihood warping)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model for morphometric similarity was trained using Bayesian linear regression with likelihood warping (B-spline, order=3, knots=5). The training set included 4310 healthy participants. The overall healthy control count across all datasets is 5169 (sum of N from Figure 1 table: 927+209+224+645+309+456+336+615+495+494+459=5169). Note: The clinical baseline N=459 includes both HC (292) and SZ (167), but this total is used for overall dataset count. For HC-only overall: approximately 5002 (5169 - 167 SZ).
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "The training set included 4310 participants and the test set 859 participants." and "Bayesian linear regression (BLR) with likelihood warping using a B-spline (spline order = 3, number of knots = 5) was used to predict morphometric similarity from a vector of covariates (age, sex, Euler number, and scanner)."
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Janssen2024.pdf.md: MATERIALS AND METHODS / Normative modeling of morphometric similarity, L117; Figure 1, L29-47

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age statistics for overall phase computed from all 11 datasets in Figure 1. Weighted mean age: (927*22.85 + 209*22.18 + 224*21.96 + 645*54.53 + 309*54.09 + 456*50.82 + 336*21.92 + 615*69.44 + 495*39.70 + 494*45.18 + 459*30.24) / 5169 = 218,088.37 / 5169 ≈ 42.19 years. Pooled SD calculated using sqrt(sum((n_i-1)*sd_i^2)/sum(n_i-1)) ≈ 17.85 years. Age range from clinical sample description: 16-68 years at baseline. Individual dataset age ranges not fully reported. Training phase specific statistics not reported separately.
